title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: THE LAST BUS
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Nadine Pruett, a hospital cook in Fargo, North Dakota.
Nadine is forty-nine, and she has never driven a car.
For twenty years, the bus took her to work. Then the city cut the route.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE BUS STOP
segments.quote: There is a certain relief in change, even though it be from bad to worse!
segments.author: Washington Irving
lines: On the last morning, Nadine was mad as a wet cat.
Lonnie, her driver, grinned and quoted Washington Irving:
There is a certain relief in change, even though it be from bad to worse!
Nadine laughed.
That night, she signed up for driving lessons.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE FIRST LESSON
segments.quote: Courage is rightly esteemed the first of human qualities because, as has been said, it is the quality which guarantees all others.
segments.author: Winston Churchill
lines: Her teacher, Brianna, was twenty-six.
Nadine gripped the wheel. She almost walked home.
Then she remembered the words of Winston Churchill:
Courage is rightly esteemed the first of human qualities because, as has been said, it is the quality which guarantees all others.
She pressed the gas. Then the brake. Brianna wore her coffee.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE ROAD TEST
segments.quote: Any man can make mistakes, but only an idiot persists in his error.
segments.author: Cicero
lines: Nadine failed her road test. Parallel parking. She ran over a cone.
She failed again. Same cone.
Her neighbor Arvid, a retired plow driver, quoted Cicero, the Roman:
Any man can make mistakes, but only an idiot persists in his error.
So she stopped guessing, learned to turn later, and passed.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE BLIZZARD
segments.quote: I can't change the direction of the wind, but I can adjust my sails to always reach my destination.
segments.author: Jimmy Dean
lines: Then came the first blizzard. Nadine slid into a snowbank.
She wanted to sell the car. Arvid pulled her out and quoted Jimmy Dean, the country singer:
I can't change the direction of the wind, but I can adjust my sails to always reach my destination.
So she bought snow tires and kitty litter for the trunk.
She drove slower than a parade. But she got there.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE SUNDAY DRIVE
segments.quote: One's destination is never a place, but rather a new way of looking at things.
segments.author: Henry Miller
lines: One Sunday, Nadine just drove.
The prairie sky looked twice as big. She thought of the writer Henry Miller:
One's destination is never a place, but rather a new way of looking at things.
She found a diner with amazing pie.
Now she goes every Sunday. For the view, she says. It's the pie.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE PASSENGER
segments.quote: As we express our gratitude, we must never forget that the highest appreciation is not to utter words, but to live by them.
segments.author: John F. Kennedy
lines: Then she heard Lonnie had retired, with no car.
She thought of the words of John F. Kennedy:
As we express our gratitude, we must never forget that the highest appreciation is not to utter words, but to live by them.
So on Thanksgiving, Nadine honked outside Lonnie's house.
Now she drives him to bowling every Thursday. He says she brakes too hard.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Welcome change. Be brave. Fix the mistake. Adjust your sails. Enjoy the ride. Give back.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Welcome change. Be brave. Fix the mistake. Adjust your sails. Enjoy the ride. Give back.
I once failed my road test too. The cone filed a complaint.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
